text:
incident-bot: Pager: High 5xx rate detected on api-gateway cluster (eu-west + us-west). 5xx > 8% over 3m, alerting oncall. metrics: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/6329991110 :rotating_light:
maya: Ack — I'm on it, opening an ops bridge now. joining: https://meet.internal/ops/6329991110
maya: Quick ask — is this global or region-specific? seeing customer tickets come in already.
liam: I'm seeing the spike originate at edge mux -> apigw fanout, mostly 502s. sample logs: ```[edge] 2026-03-17T02:32:05Z client=10.4.5.6 upstream=apigw-eu-03 status=502 path=/v1/generate```. rate higher for long-running streaming requests.
ramon: Kicking off kvcache and backend checks. No obvious pod OOMs on apigw yet. redis-kv latency healthy.
sre-ops: TL;DR: likely upstream timeouts + retry amplification at the gateway. Recommendation: disable gateway retries for streaming routes, enable backpressure (drop large clients), and shift a small percentage of traffic to dedicated pool.
jess-support: FYI AcmeCorp and BetaStream reporting 502s on API calls. Customer-impact label: paying customers affected.
maya: Executing tactical steps: 1) reduce retries -> 0 for streaming 2) add rate-limit for top clients 3) start 10% traffic shift to dedicated pool. running commands now.
maya: ```# internalctl
rbctl config set apigw.retry.streaming 0
rbctl config set apigw.ratelimit.client AcmeCorp=200r/s
rbctl traffic shift apigw eu-west->dedicated-pool --percent 10
```
liam: Noted. I'm seeing increased 504s to /v1/embeddings upstream (inference pool). Could be slow model workers causing gateway to return 504. If retries are off that should reduce amplification.
ramon: Toggled retries -> 0 (applied). Confirmed via rollout logs: rollout/apigw-config 1/1 updated.
ramon: Applied client throttle for top 5 clients. commands: ```rate-limiter apply --client AcmeCorp --limit 200```
sre-ops: Monitoring telemetry — error rate dropping from 9.1% -> 5.6% over the last 90s after changes. latency for healthy requests stable.
jess-support: Any timeline for full recovery for impacted customers? I want to reply to support tickets.
maya: If trend continues we'll increment traffic shift to 30% in 10m and keep watching. For now message support: "We applied gateway-level mitigations (retries disabled + throttles) and started routing traffic to dedicated capacity; investigating upstream inference latency. Expect progressive improvement over next 15–30m."
liam: Recommendation: capture a sampling of failing request IDs and confirm if failures map to specific inference hosts; prepping a quick grep script.
liam: ```curl -s 'https://logs.internal/query?from=6329991000&to=6329991240&q=apigw status:502' | jq '.hits[] | {req_id: .id, upstream: .upstream}'```
ramon: Ran the grep — 72% of failing reqs reference inf-host-07 and inf-host-09 in eu-west. I'm scaling inference pool and draining inf-host-07 for deeper inspection.
ramon: `kubectl scale deploy inference-eu --replicas=18` -> scaled. draining node inf-host-07 for postmortem.
sre-ops: Nice. Metrics show 5xx now ~3.2% after drain + throttles + retries off. Customer impact reduced but not fully cleared.
jess-support: Thanks. I'll update AcmeCorp + BetaStream with the mitigation note and ETA window 30m.
maya: Ops bridge: we're staying in it until the error rate stays <1% for 10m and key customers confirm. Oncall handoff in 20m to daytime rotation — @liam you'll take the daytime lead?
liam: I can take the handoff, will keep an eye on the dedicated pool and inference hosts.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated -> P2. Pager cleared for active paging, monitoring for regression.
maya: Closing loop: add incident to postmortem queue and tag inference-host-07 for hardware/OS-level deeper check. Leaving bridge; handing to liam.
liam: Copy — taking over. I'll post a 1hr update and follow up with postmortem notes.
jess-support: Marking support tickets as "mitigated, monitoring" and will reopen if errors reappear.
ramon: I'll follow up on the drained host logs and upload to /incidents/6329991110/artifacts when done.
liam: Thanks team, good quick mitigation.
maya: :white_check_mark: great job everyone.
